findings: Chapter 4 exercise (PDF 89-92, printed 86-89) solved 2026-10-29 on the owner's request (Practice, English and Roman Urdu): 10 MCQs (keyed checkpoints), 11 short answers, 7 constructed response questions, 6 comprehensive questions and 10 numerical problems, all as printed and in the book's order. Drafts for the academic review.

The book prints no MCQ key; the keys were worked out from the chapter: 4.1 a, 4.2 a, 4.3 d, 4.4 b, 4.5 b, 4.6 a, 4.7 d, 4.8 d, 4.9 d, 4.10 c. MCQ 4.6 prints its fourth option with the label (b) again; it is (d).

Book corrections: Numerical 4.1 prints 9800 watt; 9800 J is the K.E. of one bullet, and 6 bullets per minute give P = 58 800 J / 60 s = 980 W. Numerical 4.7(b) prints 11.6 %; useful work 39 200 J / input 671 400 J = 5.84 % (part (a) 671 400 J is right).

Doubtful print: Numerical 4.2 omits the unit of the solar rate ('300 per square metre', taken as 300 W m^-2). Numerical 4.9: the exponent of y is faint, read as 3/2 (it gives the printed 781.25 J); the printed unit of a (m s^-2) is not dimensionally consistent with v = a y^(3/2). The page header prints the chapter title as 'Work, Energy and Force'.

Answers beyond the chapter: Numerical 4.7 uses 1 hp = 746 W; Short 4.7 (gravitational units kg-wt m and g-wt cm, erg) is from earlier classes; Short 4.1 (elevator control and load limit) and Short 4.5 (sand leaking from the trolley, momentum) are general reasoning; Numerical 4.4 combines the vertical-circle condition of chapter 3 with energy conservation (v = sqrt(5gr)).
No figures are needed; nothing is copied from the book beyond the printed questions.
